A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TPO research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6, Table 1, and Appendix I report original T5 summarization experiments on XSum, using a reward model to simulate human feedback.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Appendix I.2 adds original results for IPO and XPO instantiations in Table 2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 3 replaces its fixed DPO update with a selectable policy optimizer, instantiated by DPO, IPO, or XPO. The UCB selection mechanism and theoretical TPO/TPS procedures remain. The added threshold comment does not establish a new mechanism: v1 already documents using 0.55 in Appendix I.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate XSum summarization with the same T5 model family and simulated human-feedback source. The additional optimizer choices do not introduce another dataset, task, population, or input environment.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained DPO comparisons, Table 2 adds iterative-IPO and iterative-XPO as evaluated no-transfer comparators, alongside their corresponding ROUGE-Lsum-only and T5-Large-only transfer baselines. This substantially broadens comparison beyond the original DPO-based methods.

E3.justification: Appendix I.2 introduces IPO/XPO experimental configurations, specifying a learning rate of 1e-5 for IPO versus the retained DPO setting of 5e-5. Other training and evaluation settings are stated to remain the same; no revision to the original DPO protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Appendix I.2 adds a check of whether transfer benefits persist when the policy-optimization component uses IPO or XPO instead of DPO. The existing source-selection investigation in Figure 2 is unchanged, rather than a newly added analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds and 95% confidence levels for Table 1, and three-trial averages for Figure 2. The new Table 2 follows the same uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds two complete sets of optimizer-specific results; final win rates against the corresponding no-transfer baselines are 55.3 ± 1.1% for IPO and 52.2 ± 1.6% for XPO. Table 1 and Figure 2 remain unchanged. Section 6 newly claims continuous decline for every source's win rate, although Figure 2 shows BERTScore increasing between iterations 2 and 3.

T1.justification: Corollary 4.4 changes from a proved no-source result using a two-phase alpha schedule to XPO-specific TPO bounds with fixed alpha = exp(-R/beta); the former appendix proof is removed. The main theorems remain. Lemma 3.1 explicitly includes source policies, but its supporting stronger bounded-ratio result already appears in v1's Appendix E.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add an explicit modularity claim: the empirical transfer mechanism can improve DPO, IPO, and XPO. The introduction also qualifies policy-class complexity independence with an exception for log-covering numbers. The central reward-transfer and self-transfer contributions remain.

C2.justification: The return from source transfer to online learning is newly emphasized in Section 6, but v1 already discusses that transition in Appendix I and escaping source-model suboptimality in Section 3.2. The theory–practice qualification in Remark G.4 and the stated larger-model and applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix I.2 supplies the IPO learning rate and explains that the iterative-XPO comparator generates both responses using the current learning policy. Best-of-N sampling, the 0.55 threshold, hardware, batch size, evaluation sampling, and code-access information were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds the IPO reference by Azar et al. (2024) and explains its relationship to the modular empirical method. Remark I.1 also distinguishes the evaluated iterative-XPO implementation from XPO's theoretical sampling design. The broader related-work discussion remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract, contribution paragraphs, and empirical-method explanation, renames the self-transfer policy from pi_OFF to pi_Dstl, and subdivides Appendix I. The overall organization remains. A previously resolved corollary cross-reference becomes 'Coro. ??' in Section 3.2.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel Table 2 and updates Figure 1's labels and caption. Algorithm 2 and existing displays shift position, including Figure 2 moving to the final appendix page. The original result table and source-selection plots retain their display content.

improvement.justification: The IPO/XPO comparisons strengthen evidence that the transfer mechanism works with different policy optimizers, and the logarithmic-complexity qualification improves precision. These are limited gains within the same XSum/T5 setting. They are tempered by removal of the earlier special-case proof, a broken corollary reference, and overstated monotonicity wording for the unchanged Figure 2.
